F5.quote: We introduce Search Arena, a crowdsourced in-the-wild evaluation platform for search-augmented LLM systems based on human preference.
F5.claim: Search Arena defined by its launch post: a crowdsourced in-the-wild evaluation platform for search-augmented LLM systems based on human preference
F5.lineage: what it is: a leaderboard of search models by human vote

F6.quote: Unlike LM-Arena or SimpleQA, our data focuses on current events and diverse real-world use cases
F6.claim: its data, unlike LM-Arena's or SimpleQA's, focuses on current events and diverse real-world use cases

F7.quote: Based on 7k human votes (03/18–04/13), Gemini-2.5-Pro-Grounding and Perplexity-Sonar-Reasoning-Pro are at the top, followed by the rest of Perplexity’s Sonar models, Gemini-2.0-Flash-Grounding, and OpenAI’s web search API models.
F7.claim: the first leaderboard, on 7k votes from 18 March to 13 April 2025: Gemini-2.5-Pro-Grounding and Perplexity-Sonar-Reasoning-Pro at the top
F7.lineage: the current board: snapshots and dates

F8.quote: Standardizing citation styles had minimal effect on rankings (see Sec. 2).
F8.claim: standardizing citation styles had minimal effect on rankings
F8.lineage: the citation finding: preference follows citation count

F9.quote: Three features show strong positive correlation with human preference: response length, citation count, and citing specific web sources like YouTube and online forum/blogs (see Sec. 3).
F9.claim: three features correlate strongly with preference: response length, citation count, citing YouTube and forums/blogs
F9.lineage: the citation finding: preference follows citation count

F10.quote: To this end, we developed search arena, aiming to (1) enable crowd-sourced evaluation of search-augmented LLMs and (2) release a diverse, in-the-wild dataset of user–system interactions.
F10.claim: its two aims: crowd-sourced evaluation of search-augmented LLMs and a released in-the-wild dataset of interactions
F10.lineage: what it is: a leaderboard of search models by human vote

F11.quote: Since our initial launch on March 18th, we’ve collected over 11k votes across 10+ models. We then filtered this data to construct 7k battles with user votes
F11.claim: launched 18 March (2025); over 11k votes across 10+ models, filtered to 7k battles
F11.lineage: genealogy: the launch, the paper, the dataset

F12.quote: To balance these considerations, we introduced “style randomization”: responses are displayed either in a standardized format or in the original format (i.e., the citation style agreed upon with each model provider).
F12.claim: style randomization: responses shown in a standardized or the provider's original citation format

F13.quote: Search Arena currently supports 11 models from three providers: Perplexity, Gemini, and OpenAI.
F13.claim: at launch, 11 models from three providers: Perplexity, Gemini, OpenAI

F14.quote: Consistent with LM Arena, we apply the Bradley-Terry (BT) model to compute model scores. The resulting BT coefficients are then translated to Elo scale
F14.claim: the score: a Bradley-Terry model over battles, its coefficients translated to the Elo scale, as in LM Arena

F15.quote: The confidence intervals are still wide, which means the leaderboard hasn’t fully settled and there’s still some uncertainty.
F15.claim: its stated limit at launch: wide confidence intervals; the leaderboard not settled

F16.quote: Controlling for citation count also results in a positive and significant coefficient (0.234, p < 0.05), suggesting a preference for responses with more cited sources.
F16.claim: citation count as a control: positive, significant coefficient (0.234, p < 0.05)
F16.lineage: the citation finding: preference follows citation count

F17.quote: When controlling for all features, only response length and citation count remain statistically significant.
F17.claim: under joint controls only response length and citation count stay significant
F17.lineage: the citation finding: preference follows citation count

F18.quote: When controlling for the number of citations, model rankings converge (i.e., multiple models share the same rank), suggesting that the number of citations is a significant factor impacting differences across models and the resulting rankings.
F18.claim: controlling for citation count, rankings converge: citation count drives differences in the rankings
F18.lineage: the citation finding: preference follows citation count

F19.quote: All models favor authoritative sources (e.g., Wikipedia, .edu, .gov domains). … OpenAI models heavily cite news sources—51.3% overall and 87.3% for Trump-related prompts.
F19.claim: all models favor authoritative sources; OpenAI's cite news heavily (51.3%; 87.3% on Trump-related prompts)

F20.quote: †We evaluate OpenAI’s web search API, which is different from the search feature in the ChatGPT product.
F20.claim: a limit: OpenAI's web search API is evaluated, not ChatGPT's search feature

F21.quote: Open participation: We are inviting model submissions from researchers and industry, and encouraging public voting.
F21.claim: open participation: model submissions invited, public voting encouraged

F22.quote: Published on 15 Apr 2025 … Last updated on 2 Aug 2025 … Mihran Miroyan*. (2025). Introducing the Search Arena: Evaluating Search-Enabled AI. https://blog.lmarena.ai/blog/2025/search-arena/
F22.claim: the post published 15 April 2025, updated 2 August 2025, cited at its lmarena.ai address
F22.lineage: genealogy: the launch, the paper, the dataset

F23.claim: the site's operator: Arena Intelligence Inc.
F23.lineage: operator: Arena, formerly LMArena and Chatbot Arena

F24.quote: [Submitted on 5 Jun 2025 (v1), last revised 2 Mar 2026 (this version, v2)] … Authors:Mihran Miroyan, Tsung-Han Wu, Logan King, Tianle Li, Jiayi Pan, Xinyan Hu, Wei-Lin Chiang, Anastasios N. Angelopoulos, Trevor Darrell, Narges Norouzi, Joseph E. Gonzalez
F24.claim: the paper: Miroyan et al. (eleven authors), v1 5 June 2025, v2 2 March 2026
F24.lineage: genealogy: the launch, the paper, the dataset

F25.quote: Search-augmented language models combine web search with Large Language Models (LLMs) to improve response groundedness and freshness. However, analyzing these systems remains challenging: existing datasets are limited in scale and narrow in scope, often constrained to static, single-turn, fact-checking questions.
F25.claim: the class and the problem: search-augmented LLMs combine web search with LLMs; existing datasets are small, narrow, static, single-turn

F26.quote: In this work, we introduce Search Arena, a crowd-sourced, large-scale, human-preference dataset of over 24,000 paired multi-turn user interactions with search-augmented LLMs.
F26.claim: Search Arena defined by its paper: a crowd-sourced human-preference dataset of over 24,000 paired multi-turn interactions with search-augmented LLMs

F27.quote: The dataset spans diverse intents and languages, and contains full system traces with around 12,000 human preference votes.
F27.claim: diverse intents and languages, full system traces, around 12,000 preference votes

F28.quote: Our analysis reveals that user preferences are influenced by the number of citations, even when the cited content does not directly support the attributed claims, uncovering a gap between perceived and actual credibility.
F28.claim: headline finding: preference follows the number of citations even when the cited content does not support the attributed claims; a gap between perceived and actual credibility
F28.lineage: the citation finding: preference follows citation count

F29.quote: Furthermore, user preferences vary across cited sources, revealing that community-driven platforms are generally preferred and static encyclopedic sources are not always appropriate and reliable.
F29.claim: preference varies by cited source: community-driven platforms generally preferred; static encyclopedic sources not always appropriate and reliable

F30.quote: We find that web search does not degrade and may even improve performance in non-search settings; however, the quality in search settings is significantly affected if solely relying on the model's parametric knowledge.
F30.claim: cross-arena finding: web search does not degrade non-search performance; parametric knowledge alone hurts search settings

F31.quote: We open-sourced the dataset to support future research. … Accepted to ICLR 2026.
F31.claim: the dataset open-sourced; the paper accepted to ICLR 2026
